turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Well, for about 6 weeks I’ve had tingling pain in the sole of my right foot that gets worse when I lift my foot up while exercising. When I stop and rest, it goes away within a few minutes, but during treadmill incline I also get right calf cramps and have to take frequent breaks.”
To better understand your symptoms, can you tell me if the tingling pain or calf cramps radiate or spread to other areas, such as your toes, ankle, or higher up your leg?
“Mostly it stays in the sole of my right foot, though the discomfort can feel a bit higher toward my ankle. The calf cramps seem limited to the right calf and don’t really spread up past the knee.”

You mentioned that the symptoms worsen with exercise and improve with rest. Have you noticed any other triggers or factors that make your symptoms better or worse, such as certain positions or activities other than exercise?

“Other than raising my foot during exercise, it’s pretty consistent—if I keep resting it improves, and when I push through it the tingling and cramps come back. I don’t really notice it getting worse with just standing still or at night, and nothing else besides that exertion seems to change it much.”
To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you've experienced any recent trauma or injury to your right foot, ankle, or leg that might be related to these symptoms?
“No, I haven’t had any injury or trauma to my right foot, ankle, or leg—this started gradually after I began exercising more regularly.”
Have you noticed any weakness or difficulty controlling your right foot or ankle, such as difficulty walking on your toes or heels?

“I haven’t noticed obvious weakness, but because it hurts and cramps during the incline I end up changing how I walk and I try not to push off too hard. I can still walk on my toes and heels, though it’s uncomfortable on that right side when I’m exercising.”
To further understand the nature of your symptoms, have you experienced any numbness, loss of sensation, or changes in your reflexes in your right foot or leg?

“I do feel some numbness along with the tingling in the sole, but it isn’t like a complete loss of sensation. I haven’t noticed any changes in my reflexes, and when I rest the symptoms improve fairly quickly.”

The symptoms you're describing, such as tingling pain in the sole of your foot that worsens with exercise and improves with rest, along with calf cramps, suggest a condition related to increased activity or pressure on the nerves or blood vessels. Given that you've started exercising more regularly and the symptoms are localized to one leg, a condition that affects the nerves or blood supply to the leg is likely.

Since you've had no trauma, the gradual onset with exercise points towards a condition that is exacerbated or triggered by physical activity. The presence of both tingling/numbness and calf cramps during exertion is particularly suggestive of a condition that involves either nerve compression or vascular insufficiency.

Considering your symptoms and their relation to exercise, I'm going to take a closer look at the evidence.
